targets.title: Responsiveness without Representation: Evidence from Minimum Wage Laws in US States
targets.evidence_quote:
We replicate and expand a recent study by Simonovits, Guess,

and Nagler (2019) to explore if its conclusion – a pronounced and uniform conservative

bias – has stood.
targets.outcome_quote:
No state had a liberal bias in 2014, and the smallest
conservative bias was in Oregon at $1. By 2021, ten states had less conservative bias

than that, and three states (California, Washington, and DC) had a liberal policy bias.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The earlier pronounced conservative bias persists on average, but the original uniform conservative pattern no longer holds: three jurisdictions now have liberal bias. Both are central to the stated retest.
